source: Morais O., Cargill C., Parke K. and Barnes T. 2020. Smallholder Pig Production Technicians' Manual. Timor-Leste Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, University of Queensland, ACIAR and the TOMAK Program (Australian Aid), Dili.
text: Heat (oestrus) in sows and gilts progresses in three stages. Early signs: general restlessness, a red and swollen vulva, and white mucus discharge. The main heat stage lasts 40–60 hours: the vulva becomes less red and swollen, mucus discharge becomes slimy and sticky (testable by stretching it between finger and thumb), the animal tends to mount or be mounted by other sows, and — most reliably — she will stand still when pressure is applied to her back (the 'standing reflex'). This is the window to mate her twice, 12–14 hours apart. In the post-oestrus stage she will no longer stand still under back pressure and the vulva swelling disappears.
caveat: This guidance comes from a Timor-Leste smallholder pig manual, not a Cambodia-specific source. Feed ingredients and general husbandry practices transfer well to Cambodia's tropical smallholder conditions, but local breed weights/ages and disease-context details may differ; confirm specifics with a local vet or extension officer where precision matters.
